column3: NKJV has “measured back,” reflecting the Textus Receptus verb; the critical text has simply “it will be measured.”
Close to the Greek; “splinter” and “beam” are rendered “speck” and “plank.”
NKJV begins with “Because,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has an exclamation, “How narrow …!” “Compressed” is rendered “difficult.”
NKJV has “I will liken him,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “he will be like.” “Words” is rendered “sayings.”
Close to the Greek; “the crowds” is rendered “the people.”
NKJV has “the scribes,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “their scribes.”
